item.title: Bridges & Brunch with Strasburg Scooter Tours — Fri Oct 2 — Strasburg Scooter Tours
item.description:
Experience a relaxing morning ride through the back roads of Amish Country in Lancaster County, PA. Along the way to a 19th century covered bridge, enjoy the scenery of rolling hills, breathtaking views, and our Amish neighbors going about their daily routines. Itinerary Duration: 1.5-2 hours Some of our past tours have included:
A guided tour of one of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges An opportunity for a close up of daily life in Amish Country $10 dining voucher to one of two of Strasburg’s favorites brunch spots, Casey Jones’ Restaurant and Speckled Hen*
And each trip is unique, so you never know what we might have in store for you! *Unfortunately, we regret to inform you that some of the food offerings on the tour may not be considered ‘Kosher.’ We apologize for any inconvenience.
Source: Discover Lancaster

item.title: Lititz Game Club at the Lititz Public Library — Wed Oct 7, 4:30 PM
item.description:
Central PA Game Club A place for people to come together and play tabletop games. Whether you enjoy casual games like Uno and Scrabble, gateway games like Catan, Wingspan, and Ticket to Ride, or more strategic games like Scythe and Terraforming Mars, we have plenty of fun games to play. A game library with a wide selection of games is available, but feel free to bring your own (family-friendly) games as well!
Source: Meetup: Central PA Game Club

item.title: Dillsburg Game Night - Calvary Methodist Church in the Family Center — Wed Oct 7, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Central PA Game Club Dillsburg Game Night meets every Wednesday from 6:30-9:30pm for casual tabletop games. We’ve been going strong since 2016, and most Wednesdays you’ll find about 30-40 gamers who love to learn and teach new games. It’s a great group of friendly people.
Given the timeframe, most of the games played are light to medium Euros, although many of us also love card games (including trick-taking games) and party games. We have a library of about 200 games available to play, and people typically bring their own games as well.
We also run long game days (typically every other month, usually a Saturday 2-9pm) and other special events. Join us on Facebook or Discord for more information about those.
Attendees do not often RSVP on Meetup. It may show 1 person is coming but we have 40 people every Wednesday and will cancel the event if it is not happening. Feel free to message with questions.
Cost: Free Who: All Ages (15 and under must be accompanied by an adult) When: Every

item.title: LFS Women’s Gathering — Sat Oct 17, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Lancaster Freethought Society **Join us for the first LFS Women's Gathering: Lunch at Loxley's!** This is simply a chance for women in and around LFS to spend some time together — to meet women we may not know well, catch up with women we do, share a meal, talk, laugh, and enjoy one another’s company. There’s no business meeting and no required agenda. We can talk about whatever interests us: our lives, ideas, books, politics, culture, what’s happening in Lancaster, what we’ve been thinking about lately — or anything else that comes up around the table. We’ll also talk a little about whether we’d like to make this a regular gathering and, if so, what **we** would like it to be. For our first get-together, we’re meeting at Loxley’s — an especially fun place to begin, with its Robin Hood and Sherwood Forest theme. And since every good Sherwood Forest gathering needs her: **Maid Marian is welcome at our table.**
Source: Meetup: Lancaster Freethought Society

item.title: Trivia Night at Southern Market - Meet People Lancaster team — Wed Oct 21, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Meet People Lancaster Do you love trivia nights, but want to avoid the hassle of trying to wrangle up enough friends to field a team? Come play for a Meet People Lancaster team and make some new friends along the way! Cost: FREE Bar & food stations are all walk up. You’ll be on your own tab for the night. Host: Elizabeth Chapman Please try to get there by 6:30PM, so we can get situated at a couple tables. Trivia starts at 7PM. If you come early, you’ll have time to mingle and get some food before trivia starts.
Location: 100 S Queen St, Lancaster, PA 17603 How to find the group: Our “usual” trivia spot is the tables in front of Gloomy Rooster/Noodle King in the front left corner. We will also have a few yellow MPL signs!

item.description:

item.title: Being One Online Spiritual Support Group — Mon Oct 26, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Being One Center in Lancaster County Life can be frustrating and distressing! Sometimes we just feel overwhelmed, insecure, or lost!
The good news is, you're not alone!
We warmly invite you to check-in and connect with community in our Online Spiritual Support Group. In each meeting, we will discuss our current stressors and see how we can positively cope using our spiritual tools to overcome these challenges.
Together we can help each other grow and expand our consciousness for these high vibrational times.
Donations Greatly Appreciated!
This Event is lovingly hosted By Anna Bojczuk. Anna is a Registered nurse with over 40 years of experience as well as a gifted Energy worker. Anna is also long-time volunteer and inspiration in the Being One Center Community.
Donations to the Being One Center are greatly appreciated (https://www.paypal.com/donate?token=AzIxMnj72R-pxLPP0cGQILM7OPiZs5zbsOdxGA7LFH60Wkr_0YcLATVAkIHYVjrFl4PP36X2GkDEJbaM)

Join us for an evening of Klezmer and Jewish music. Klezmer music is traditional instrumental music of the Ashkenazi Jews. Meet the musicians; Christopher Brooks was born and raised in Brooklyn, New York. He began studying the violin at PS 8 in Brooklyn Heights and at the Third Street Music School. Attending the New School of Music in Philadelphia, Mr. Brooks studied violin with Jascha Brodsky and Geoffrey Michaels. He has played chamber music and been a member of numerous orchestras. Laurie Haines Reese is a cellist dedicated to creating and performing music—especially new music—that explores the cello’s creative possibilities. An accomplished classical musician with a lifelong curiosity about what else the cello can do, she is equally at home in folk, jazz, improvisatory, and experimental music.
